transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Start: 10:30 AM EDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Rossi (CTO - Vanguard Pathology), Samir Patel (Infra), Marta Alvarez (Security), Luis Garza (Lab Ops)

Summary:
Quick feasibility discovery for an air-gapped / dark-site on-prem deployment. Customer needs: no outbound internet from inference nodes, signed offline updates, strict audit logs, limited on-site GPU SKUs, and alignment on maintenance windows. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, image delivery, and key management.

Topics:
- Air-gapped deployment constraints and update cadence
- Hardware inventory, power/cooling, GPU compatibility
- KMS/HSM and key-injection strategy for offline nodes
- Compliance requirements (SOC2/HIPAA/ISO) and audit logs
- Pilot scope and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for blocking time. quick intros, and then priya will run through the technical constraints.
[00:12] Elena: sure, thanks. um we appreciate you fitting us in. we run pathology inference in a physical lab facility, 100% isolated network, USB-only ingress for updates, so this is about feasibility.
[00:25] Priya (Redwood SE): great, thanks elena. to set expectations, we support a private on-prem package that can run entirely air-gapped — but there are tradeoffs around how updates are delivered and how K M S is handled. one question up front: do you have an existing H S M or KMS appliance on-site?
[00:42] Marta (Security): we do have an HSM in the data room; it's an nCipher box. everything that needs keys must be signed by that H S M. we cannot allow outbound key escrow.
[00:54] Jordan: okay makes sense — so BYO-HSM scenario. good.
[00:58] Samir (Infra): also important: our racks are older, single-phase power limits, and we currently have two A40s and one A100 across the cluster. procurement for new GPUs will be tricky for Q3.
[01:12] Priya: thanks. the runtime can work on A40 and A100; H100 gives best perf but not mandatory. we will need kernel compat checks and some drivers. firmware updates for GPUs will have to be coordinated.
[01:28] Luis (Lab Ops): when you say "updates", do you mean entire OS images, or can you do delta patches? we prefer smaller packages because of the USB workflow.
[01:36] Priya: we typically provide signed image bundles. for air-gapped sites we support two mechanisms: full signed images delivered on media, or a delta patch flow if you have a secure media transfer agent. deltas reduce transfer time but add complexity.
[01:49] Elena: delta sounds nice but our QA wants deterministic rollbacks; full images are easier for audit.
[01:56] Jordan: noted. full images + signed manifests are the default for these environments. we'll include an offline update playbook. link: https://redwood.internal/security-pack (placeholder, will send public pack)
[02:08] Marta: we need to see audit log retention and how you collect _events_ from nodes when there's no outbound network.
[02:16] Priya: good question. in air-gapped mode we persist signed logs locally and then we have a secure pull process—usually a read-only transfer to a forensic host in the DMZ during maintenance windows. logs are signed and checksummed.
[02:29] Marta: ok that could work, but we need to make sure logs can't be tampered with.
[02:33] Priya: yep, we use chain-signed entries and optional H S M sealing.
[02:40] Samir: about resource limits: our NVLink infrastructure is limited — we don't have multi-node NVLink topology. will that affect throughput?
[02:47] Priya: it depends on model size and batch strategy. for larger LLMs, absence of NVLink means inter-GPU communication hits PCIe and that increases latency; we can recommend quantized model variants or smaller context sizes. also continuous batching may be constrained.
[03:05] Jordan: can you give a sense of the S L A you would require?
[03:09] Elena: latency isn't the top priority — predictability is. 95th percentile tail under 1.2s for typical pathology inference is our target. throughput must handle peak batch loads during lab shifts.
[03:21] Priya: okay predictable tail is something we tune for with model variants and batching profiles. in air-gapped, caching strategies like prefix K V cache help reduce token generation cost — though K V cache was mis-heard in notes earlier as K V cash but it's the same thing.
[03:39] Samir: other security items — S S O / S A M L integration for the console? we have an internal identity provider but no outbound SAML to cloud.
[03:48] Jordan: the private control plane supports SAML/SSO in a federated mode and we can host the control plane on-prem or in a customer VPC with connector. for fully air-gapped customers we run a local control plane instance.
[04:00] Marta: do you support RBAC and per-key audit trails?
[04:03] Priya: yes R B A C is supported. audit trails are tied to token IDs and we can configure retention. again for air-gapped sites retention is local until a permitted export.
[04:14] Elena: two practical questions: 1) how do we get images into the site? 2) what's the test/pilot scope?
[04:20] Jordan: image delivery options — signed USB drives physically delivered by your ops team; air-gapped transfer appliance via an approved intermediary; or couriered sealed media. we'll provide a manifest and signature verification steps you run in the data room.
[04:32] Luis: and can we verify signatures on a read-only host? we don't want to run verification tools on production inference nodes.
[04:38] Priya: yes we expect verification on an isolated host that has the H S M provisioning key. after verification, the image is mounted to compute nodes via a secure process. we'll document the exact commands.
[04:49] Elena: pilot scope — we want to test a single rack of inference capacity with one model (pathology triage model), two GPUs per node, and rollout to a subset of internal users. timeframe ideally before end of Q2.
[05:00] Jordan: that aligns well with a small Dedicated reservation or a Private on-prem pilot. we'll propose a 6-week pilot plan: week 1 hardware map, week 2 image prep & signing, week 3 deployment, week 4 perf tuning, week 5 validation with your QA, week 6 wrap and handoff.
[05:17] Samir: constraint: we only have one maintenance window per month (2 AM Sunday) with a 2-hour window. can you get a deployment done in that time?
[05:26] Priya: full image installation in a 2-hour window could be tight if it's a full OS + model bundle. we can stage some prechecks and pre-provision images so that the actual switch is fast. the kit we deliver includes a checklist for staged installs.
[05:42] Marta: also we need traceability for firmware and BIOS. any update must be approved by our firmware governance team.
[05:48] Priya: understood — firmware rollouts are separate and we will not touch BIOS without explicit sign-off. we'll provide a firmware manifest and expected hashes.
[05:59] Elena: what about model updates? we will have regular model retraining cycles; how do we push new weights?
[06:06] Jordan: model weights are delivered as signed artifacts. we recommend off-line retrain orchestration where your ML infra produces a signed bundle that the ops team transfers through the same media flow. we can assist with a versioning scheme and test harness.
[06:20] Luis: about costs — is private deployment more expensive than dedicated?
[06:24] Jordan: on-prem private has an enterprise license + support fee, and there may be integration professional services. Dedicated is a managed reserved capacity in our datacenter — cheaper to start, but if you need zero outbound or BYO-HSM then private on-prem is necessary.
[06:39] Elena: any compliance gaps you foresee for HIPAA and our internal audit?
[06:44] Marta: plus we need ISO 27001 evidence.
[06:47] Priya: we can provide SOC2 reports and ISO materials; HIPAA controls depend on contract terms and logging retention. we'll include a compliance mapping doc in the security pack.
[06:58] Jordan: i'll include a redwood -> vanguard compliance matrix and highlight any control gaps.
[07:03] Samir: one last technical: can the runtime run without CUDA networking enabled? some of our servers are in a restricted firmware mode.
[07:11] Priya: yes, it can run in a CUDA-limited environment but performance will vary. we can run CPU fallback paths for smaller models, and recommend quantization to reduce GPU memory pressure.
[07:24] Elena: ok thanks — that was the main technical check.
[07:28] Jordan: great, to recap: we'll send security pack and offline update playbook, priya will prepare a hardware/image checklist, samir will share GPU list and rack limits, marta will define compliance acceptance criteria, and we will propose a pilot plan and pricing.
[07:45] Luis: sounds good. when can we expect the docs?
[07:48] Jordan: i'll send the initial packet by Friday (2026-04-16) and priya will follow with the checklist.
[07:55] Elena: thanks everyone.
[07:57] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the hardware mapping call. bye.

End of call.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearing of acronyms (H S M, K V cache transcribed as K V cash), speaker labeling may be approximate in a couple spots.
